One thing stopped me from just resuming cleanly, though: the frozen v1 spec contains two directly contradictory statements. Your recorded answer says *"do not delete anything,"* and the Requirements/Validation Contract are built entirely around a read-only, non-mutating scan. But the spec also carries an "Executor Note (unsourced)" saying *"Executor may delete duplicates."* There's no citation, no approval trail, and nothing else in the record that authorizes deletion — it just sits there contradicting the answer you gave.

Because that note bears directly on what an executor is allowed to do to your files, I can't quietly drop it or quietly honor it. So: is that note stale/wrong and safe to discard (keeping the report strictly read-only, per your recorded answer), or does it reflect a real later decision to allow deletion that just never got written down properly — and if the latter, what's the actual authorization/source for it?
